The statement signals a pivot to patience while reaffirming confidence in growth and employment—consistent with flexible inflation targeting and smoothed, rule-like behavior documented by Clarida, Galí, and Gertler. Emphasis on expected conditions and “muted inflation pressures” aligns with forecast-targeting frameworks (Svensson and Woodford) and Taylor-rule-style data dependence, implying no urgency to tighten further. Operationally, holding IOER at 2.40% and using ON RRP to maintain the 2.25–2.50% funds-rate range reflects the post-2008 floor system (Goodfriend; interest on reserves), showing firm rate control without additional restraint. With business fixed investment moderating and market-based inflation compensation lower, the “patient” forward guidance is a modestly dovish, risk-management response while longer-run expectations remain anchored. Overall tone: cautiously dovish, supportive of continued expansion with inflation near target.
